descriptionChirho: The Nifal stem sense of שׁאה meaning 'to roar,' 'to be in tumult,' or 'to make a din,' describing loud, chaotic noise. The translations emphasize sound and commotion: Hindi गरजती हैं/गरजता है (garajtī haiṅ/garajtā hai, 'they roar/it roars'), Spanish braman ('they bellow'), Korean 소란하도다/소란하나 (soran-hadoda/soran-hana, 'they are tumultuous'), Swahili yanayovuma/wanavuma ('that which rumbles/they rumble'), Arabic تَضِجُّ (taḍijju, 'they clamor'). Used in prophetic and wisdom literature to describe the turbulent noise of nations or cosmic upheaval (Isaiah 17:12-13), distinct from the desolation sense of the same root.

labelChirho: to be laid waste, become desolate (Qal/Nifal)
descriptionChirho: The Qal perfect and Nifal imperfect passive sense of שׁאה describing a state of devastation or desolation, where a place is ruined or laid waste. The translations uniformly point to destruction rather than noise: Spanish sean devastadas/quede desolada ('may they be devastated/may it remain desolate'), Hindi उजड़ जाएं/उजड़ जाए (ujaṛ jā'eṅ/ujaṛ jā'e, 'may they be ruined'), Arabic خَرِبَت/تَخرَبُ (kharibat/takhrabu, 'it was ruined/it will be ruined'), Korean 황폐해지면 (hwangpye-haejimyeon, 'when it becomes desolate'), Swahili zikiwa tupu/itakuwa tupu ('if they are empty/it will be empty'). This intransitive/stative desolation sense contrasts with both the acoustic 'roar' sense and the causative Hifil.

The Hifil infinitive construct of שׁאה expressing the causative action of actively making something desolate or bringing devastation upon it. The causative force is evident across translations: English to make desolate/to make-desolate, Spanish para desolación/para asolar ('for desolation/to devastate'), Hindi उजाड़ने के लिए (ujāṛne ke li'e, 'for the purpose of laying waste'), Arabic لِيُخَرِّبَ/لِتَخْرِيبِ (li-yukharriba/li-takhrībi, 'to destroy/for destruction' — both causative Form II), Korean 폐허로 만들도록/황폐시키는 것으로 (pyeheo-ro mandeul-dorok/hwangpye-sikineun geos-euro, 'so as to make ruins/by causing desolation'), Swahili kuharibu/kubomoa ('to destroy/to demolish'). This active causative stands apart from the passive/stative 'be desolate' sense.
